why: A (universes at 0) has seven conjuncts: SEPLoc.theorem_10_3_10 ([D] is an isomorphism of SEP(F⁻¹) when Ψ is a strong bundle equivalence, and every two-sided inverse is [D.symm hΨ]), isIso_of_isGeneralizedIso, inv_homMk, SDiagram.equiv_comp_symm / equiv_symm_comp (D ∘ D⁻¹ ≈ 1, D⁻¹ ∘ D ≈ 1), isEquivalence_base_of_isIso (the base half of the converse) and the example isIso_homMk_negDiagram. B says that for such D, [D ∘ revB D] = [1_W] and [revB D ∘ D] = [1_W'], with revB D h = D.symm h by rfl. A ⇒ B is equiv_comp_symm and equiv_symm_comp with cls_eq_cls_of_equiv. B ⇒ A: B's equations are homMk D ≫ homMk D⁻¹ = 𝟙 and the reverse, by rfl. They give IsIso, uniqueness of the inverse, isIso_of_isGeneralizedIso and inv_homMk, and with the non-item cls_eq_cls_iff they give the two Equiv statements and the example. The one extra in A is isEquivalence_base_of_isIso: if [D] is an isomorphism then ψ is an equivalence. That is part of the converse, which B (the text's one direction) does not address. It is re-proved outright, as in the project, in two lines from the non-item EPLoc.isIso_homMk_iff (Theorem 10.3.10 for ep-groupoids) via baseFunctor. On the text's direction the two sides say the same thing.
